routes.name: Greenhow Hill
routes.description: A climb out of Pateley Bridge in Nidderdale, to one of the highest villages in England. This route takes in four more Dales climbs.

routes.name: Sa Calobra
routes.description: A famous climb in the Serra de Tramuntana. 10 km of hairpins averaging 7 %, including a 270-degree spiral that passes under itself.

routes.name: Alpe d'Huez
routes.description: A ski resort in the French Alps, and the most famous climb in the Tour de France. 13.8 km at over 8 % from Bourg d’Oisans, with 21 hairpins numbered down to the summit.

routes.name: Rosedale Chimney
routes.description: One of the steepest surfaced roads in England, climbing out of Rosedale onto the moor. Named after the ironstone kiln chimney that stood at the top until 1972.

routes.name: Settle to Grassington
routes.description: A route between Ribblesdale and Wharfedale over Malham Moor. It climbs out of Settle and drops fast into Grassington.

routes.name: Box Hill
routes.description: A chalk hill on the North Downs, climbed by the Zig Zag Road. Used for the 2012 London Olympic road race, which lapped it 9 times.

routes.name: Koppenberg
routes.description: A cobbled lane out of Melden, and a national monument. 600 m averaging 10 % and pitching to 22 %, which has put plenty of riders off their bikes in the Tour of Flanders.

routes.name: Montjuïc
routes.description: A circuit on the hill above Barcelona, climbing to the castle and dropping back through the park. The Volta a Catalunya has finished here every year since 2013, seven laps of it.
